decisions.reason: The arbitrary-carrier construction is already explicitly supplied in the Definition by spectral-lemma steps 2.1–7.1 and the nondegenerate C0 theorem, whose Statement has no separability restriction. Those steps work for each vector on arbitrary H, since N=R^D is sigma-finite and continuous vector orbits are separable. The missing direct deps edge is a nonfatal dependency declaration defect; added that edge and its owning manifest mirror without changing the Definition.

Step 4.1 invokes a countable basis on O without establishing its subspace topology is second countable. This is a nonfatal local gap: step 2.1 already supplies an equivariant Borel isomorphism to the second-countable homogeneous quotient X. Repaired the support argument on X using F9, covariance, countable additivity and transitivity, then applied imprimitivity to both separable summands. The section cocycle, spectral concentration, direct-sum contradiction and orbit/little-group equivalence remain valid; Statement unchanged.

The measure is genuinely Radon: Mackey proof step 2.1 explicitly chooses it on the homogeneous quotient from its F5. In this application the quotient is homeomorphic to the compact sphere, so the pushed measure is finite and full-support; disjoint nonempty caps give nonzero orthogonal L2 sections. The local F2 omitted that essential qualification. Repaired F2 to cite the exact proof construction and retain strongly continuous unitary qualifiers; classification, rotation stabilizers, D=3 phases and signs, D=2 trivial stabilizers, and nontrivial translations remain valid. Statement unchanged.

F7 guarantees continuity only after its inducing representation is strongly continuous. The omitted verification is elementary, not a failure of the classification: invariance of chi_p under K_p gives multiplicativity, and the displayed norm bound reduces strong continuity of chi_p(a)theta(h) to continuity of chi_p and strong continuity of theta. Added that argument before applying F7; the forward cone-invariance implication, disjoint-orbit PVM converse, zero orbit and conjugate little-group equivalence remain sound. Statement unchanged.

F2 omitted the classification supplier's strong-continuity hypothesis, so it overstates the cited result. Added strongly continuous in F2. The actual theta_s(r)=exp(isr) is continuous, unitary and irreducible on C; induction at p=0 is from the whole group, translations are trivial, its PVM is concentrated at zero, and evaluation at r=pi/s gives -1. The example itself and its dependencies remain unchanged.

False positive: the descent supplier explicitly declares axiom_use: AC is inherited from the Mackey induction classification and Schur's lemma; its A1 and proof step 2.1 also identify AC in induction-action and Schur suppliers. Hence the example accurately inherits AC through both F2 and F3 even though the descent Statement does not repeat it. The continuous scalar character gives theta(z^N)=exp(2pi i N sqrt2); descent requires N sqrt2 integer, contradicted by the parity proof of irrationality for every N>=1. No edit warranted.

The rejection's AC rationale is not correct: both F2 and F3 explicitly inherit AC in axiom_use and their Facts/Proof, so A1 remains unchanged. Nevertheless the assigned item has a confirmed nonfatal defect independently identified by the digest: F2 says every representation is one displayed character, whereas C^2 with the trivial action is a counterexample. Restricted F2 to irreducible strongly continuous unitary representations. The proof already uses continuous one-dimensional characters, separates signs by values i and -i, and computes the independent phase exp(2pi i alpha) with descent exactly N alpha integer. Thus the actual item defect is fully repaired without weakening the Example.
